sections.translation:
## Streaming Services Summary The UX18 consoles can generate **two independent audio streams** and decode one incoming audio stream. - **Streaming 1 (outgoing)**
Uses the **RTP** protocol, ideal for a link to the **transmitter site (STL)**. - **Streaming 2 (outgoing)**
Compatible with **Shoutcast/Icecast servers** for internet broadcasting. - **Streaming 3 (incoming)**
Can be **RTP** or a **public HTTP stream**.
When this function is enabled, the received audio is **automatically decoded and switched**, replacing the **AES-1** input. - **Remote monitoring:** The UX18 incorporates a **WebRTC service** that allows you to listen to the audio remotely from the **WEB Control Interface**, whether accessed locally or externally via the Internet.
sections.title: Resúmen de los servicios de streaming

sections.translation:
## Streaming Services Configuration This is done from the **SETTINGS** screen, under the **STREAMING** option. It requires the ADMIN profile.
STREAMING launches the Streaming Interface Access screen. It displays a **summary of the status of audio transmission and reception streams**, and allows access to other configuration instances: - **STREAM CFG** → Access to the streaming services configuration. - **SYSTEM** → Access to the LAN configuration for the UX18's streaming services
(not to be confused with the WEB remote control LAN configuration). ---
sections.title: Configuración de los servicios de streaming

sections.translation:
### UP-STREAM (TX) - Icecast/Shoutcast

The **UP-STREAM** tab allows you to configure an **Icecast** or **Shoutcast** type broadcast server to publish the program signal.

- **RUN/STOP**: Enables or disables sending the streaming when changes are confirmed by pressing **APPLY**.
  <Tip>
    To optimize system resources, keep it stopped when the service is not in use.
  </Tip>
- **PROTOCOL**: Defines whether the server is Icecast or Shoutcast type.
- **SERVER IP**: Destination IP address of the server.
- **PORT**: TCP listening port of the server.
- **MOUNTPOINT**: Unique name that identifies the stream on the server.
- **Stream NAME**: Name that identifies the stream.
- **PASSWORD**: Access key for publishing (if applicable).
- **CODEC**: Audio transmission format (Opus or MP3).
- **QUALITY**: Bit rate for encoding.
- **APPLY**: Applies and saves the changes and starts or stops the broadcast (according to the RUN/STOP state).

<Note>
  The configuration parameters for Icecast/Shoutcast are provided by the server provider.
</Note>
sections.title: UP-STREAM (TX) - Icecast/Shoutcast

sections.translation: ### Audio Processing for Streaming Pressing the **PROCESS** icon accesses the audio processor, which includes **level normalization** and **bass enhancement**. This processing only affects the *streaming* for **Icecast/Shoutcast**.
sections.title: Procesado de audio para streaming

sections.translation:
#### Normalizer Reduces the signal's dynamic range and adjusts the level to a constant value, achieving a more consistent sound without volume jumps. - **Target LUFS**: Determines the target level for the streaming signal (± 1 LU).
It is adjusted based on the content type: - **-21 to -19 LU** → Signals with large level variations, without prior control (example: uncompressed microphones). - **-18 to -15 LU** → Mixed music and speech signals, using compressors on the microphone channels to limit the dynamic range. - **-14 to -12 LU** → Signals already heavily compressed (music). - **Style**: Defines the normalizer's action times.
Possible values: _slow_, _normal_, _fast_. - _Slow_: recommended when there are large volume variations. - _Fast_: useful for normalizing previously compressed signals.
sections.title: Normalizer

sections.translation:
#### Bass Boost

Applies a bass boost to the *streaming* signal.

- **FREQ.** → Cutoff frequency; the boost is applied below this frequency.
- **ACTION** → Adjusts the amount of boost applied.

<Tip>
  **Recommendation**: Use *Bass Boost* for speech-focused broadcasts to achieve voices with more impactful low frequencies.
</Tip>

---
sections.title: Bass Boost

sections.translation: ### RTP LINK The **RTP LINK** tab allows you to configure the streaming output to a specific IP address, for example, to send the program signal to a transmitter site (**STL**). Implementing an RTP link requires advanced knowledge of network configuration. - **ENABLE/DISABLED**: Enables or disables RTP streaming when changes are confirmed by pressing **APPLY**. To optimize system resources, keep it disabled when the service is not in use. - **DESTINATION ADDRESS**: Destination IP address. - **PORT**: TCP transmission port. - **CODEC**: Audio format for RTP (**PCM** / **MP3**). - **QUALITY**: MP3 bitrate or PCM sampling frequency. - **GPO**: Enables sending **Tally Light** signals via TCP/IP for compatible Solidyne equipment. - **Studio A and B** (lines 1 and 2 respectively) - **Studio B and A** (reversed order) - **A\+B** (the signal is activated on both lines, whichever studio is active) ---
sections.title: RTP LINK

sections.translation:
### Down-Stream (RX) Allows configuration of an incoming stream. When the **DOWN-STREAM** module is active, the decoded audio is sent internally to the **AES-1** input, which is renamed to **STREAM-1**.
In this mode, the AES-1 connector on the rear panel is disabled. - **RUN/STOP**
Starts or stops the stream decoding when changes are confirmed with **APPLY**. To optimize system resources, keep it stopped when the service is not in use. - **PROTOCOL**
Defines the type of incoming stream. The following formats are supported: - Public **HTTP** and **MMS** streams encoded in PCM 16 (44.1/48 kHz), MP3, or Opus. - **RTP** streams in PCM 16 (44.1 kHz) and MP3. - **SERVER URL/IP**
Name or IP address of the server generating the stream. - **PORT**
TCP port through which the stream enters.
Default value: **0**. - **MOUNTPOINT**
Unique name identifying the stream. - **APPLY**
Applies the configuration changes. **Step-by-step** Download a [step-by-step guide for configuring an incoming stream](/unidex/unidex_appnote_downstream). ---
sections.title: Down-Stream (RX)

sections.translation:
### REMOTE PLAYER

The **WEB Remote Control Interface** allows listening to the console's audio via a **WebRTC** service.
sections.title: REMOTE PLAYER

sections.translation:
#### Audio Format

- Encoding: **Opus**
- Configurable bitrate: **128 to 320 kbps**
sections.title: Formato de Audio

sections.translation:
#### Operation on the local network When accessed from a terminal on the **LAN**, no advanced configuration is required.
The remote player will play the audio directly over the local network.
sections.title: Funcionamiento en red local

sections.translation:
#### Operation via Internet

To access audio from the **WEB Control Interface** over the Internet, the network must implement:

- **Symmetric NAT**
- **TURN server**

> If these services are not available, a warning message will appear in the player.

---
sections.title: Funcionamiento vía Internet

sections.translation:
### SERVICES CFG

The **Services Configuration** screen allows you to assign audio sources to the streaming services.

| Service | Assigned Audio Source | Additional Configuration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **STREAM-1** | **Program** signal present at the **AES3-1 PGM** output | Level adjustable in `SETTINGS → OUTPUTS → AES-1/STREAM-1` |
| **STREAM-2** | Can be assigned to **PGM**, **REC**, **AUX**, **VBUS**, **STUDIO**, **CUE** or **Talk-Back** | Configurable in `SETTINGS → OUTPUTS → STREAM-2` |
sections.title: SERVICES CFG

sections.translation:
#### Operational Notes

- The **ENABLE** column allows you to start or stop each service.
- It is recommended to **keep stopped** any services that are not in use to optimize system resources.

---
sections.title: Notas operativas

sections.translation: ### Streaming System General network settings for the **Streamer UX18** module (do not confuse with the web control access). By default, the IP address operates in dynamic mode (DHCP). The assigned address is displayed on the main screen as **STREAM IP**.
sections.title: Streaming System
